articles.author: Chris Swan
articles.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS. By Chris Swan

articles.title: 尺寸暴涨！比亚迪新一代海鸥太超标了，还只要 6.59 万元
articles.author: 李华
articles.summary: 比亚迪新一代海鸥的尺寸，竟然都快赶上海豚了。 原先海鸥的车身长度只有 3780 毫米，属于标准的微型车，而现在，它的车长暴涨到了 4205 毫米，车宽和车高分别来到了 1810 毫米和 1570 毫米，轴距甚至有 2650 毫米，也就比现款海豚智驾版短了 50mm。 如今的海鸥，已经跳出了微型车的级别，成了一个正儿八经的五座车型。 尺寸加大只是海鸥换代的第一步，底盘的变化更加明显。 变化最大的是它的驱动形式，新一代海鸥舍弃了前置电机，改成了后置后驱；后悬架也从原本的扭力梁非独立悬架，换成了多连杆独立悬架。 虽然车身更长、轴距更大，但它的最小转弯半径依然做到了 4.95 米，保留了在狭窄街巷里掉头泊车的灵活性。 动力上，新一代海鸥用的是一台 95kW 的电机，峰值扭矩 130N·m，最快能够跑到 150km/h。电池也同步换成了第二代刀片电池，官方公布的百公里能耗为 9.0kWh，还支持「9 分钟充好」的比亚迪闪充。 辅助驾驶配置同样有了新的选装项——激光雷达，加上天神之眼 B 辅助驾驶系统，如今的海鸥已经能够支持城市和高快道路的领航辅助，同时还配有 6 个安全气囊和高速防爆胎稳定系统，安全性也有所提升。 尺寸变大了，储物能力自然也有所提升。 对于海鸥来说，后置后驱布局带来的最大好处，就是释放了前舱空间，车头多出了一个 94 升的前备箱。 与此同时，后面的行李箱最大扩展容积能够达到了 1380 升（后排折叠），后排坐垫下方还挖出了合计 24 升的小抽屉。 新一代海鸥的内饰也比以前精致了不少，中控台放了一块 15.6 英寸的悬浮屏，内置 DiLink 150 车机，下方的副仪表台带有一个 50W 的风冷无线充电面板。 更令人意外的是，现在海鸥的前排两张座椅都支持电动调节和加热、通风。 *说到这个，今天刚好试了最近话题度挺高的 smart 精灵...

articles.title: 电池自燃直接赔新车？理想发布自研电池「连山」，理想 i6 首发搭载
articles.author: 李华
articles.summary: 理想终于发布了他们的自研电池。 在昨晚的发布会上，这块名为「连山」的动力电池，作为理想全新三电体系的核心正式亮相。按照理想的规划，几天后上市的 2026 款理想 i6 将成为这块电池的首发车型。 连山电池带来的性能提升，首先体现在续航与环境适应能力上。 换上这块电池后，2026 款理想 i6 在 CLTC 工况下的续航来到了 780km，比现款车型提升了 8%。 除了账面上的综合续航，理想还花了不少篇幅来讲这块电池的低温表现。 在冬天，磷酸铁锂电池普遍容易出现电量估算不准的问题，但理想表示，在自研电量算法和整车余热回收系统的配合下，连山电池的续航能多出来 30 公里。 按照现场公布的规划，后续还会有一轮专门针对极寒工况的 OTA 升级，号称能为 -20°C 的低温环境带来 10 公里左右的续航提升。 发布会的另一个重点落在了安全上，理想针对日常用车容易碰到的底盘磕碰与积水路况，列出了一套包含防磕碰、防进水在内的六道防线。 根据官方公布的测试数据，连山电池的单颗电芯即便遭受 500 焦耳冲击也不会起火。而在消费者最关心的热失控方面，哪怕电芯在 50°C 高温下发生热失控，整个电池包仍能坚持 24 小时不起火。 除了物理层面的防护，理想还提到了全生命周期的监测机制，号称每颗电芯的制造数据都会保留 20 年。另外，通过车端与云端的协同运算，系统还能在潜在异常恶化之前，提前 72 小时检测出风险并发出预警。 整场发布会讨论度最高的，还是理想给出的「兜底方案」： 要是自燃了，就赔一辆新车；车辆若因碰撞起火，理想则会为用户补齐车损险保额与实际理赔金额之间的差额。 总之就是不能让用户掏钱。 不过这项兜底目前只围绕车辆本身展开，至于事故可能引发的人员伤害，理想并未提及。...

articles.summary: Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. articles.author: Jenny Lea; Max Brosnahan; Matthew Conroy
articles.summary: AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online.That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML — they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it.Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products. Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable. articles.summary: 21499 元的 iPhone Duo，加上 86749 元的 Mac Studio，两台设备加起来超过 10 万元。 APPSO 想用这两台苹果史上最贵的手机和电脑，打造一个这个时代最优雅的「智能个人中心」。 256G 内存，1.2TB/s 内存带宽的超强算力 Mac Studio 留在家里，负责运行模型和执行 Agent 任务。 出门只带一台 Duo，需要的时候掏出手机，就能看看家里的电脑忙到哪了，或者再给它派点活。 为此我们还专门做了一个深度适配 iPhone Duo 的 App，针对合盖、半折悬停以及完全展开三种不同的形态，分别设计了对应 Agent 的不同工厂场景。 iPhone Duo + Mac Studio，苹果 AI 王炸组合 先把 Mac Studio 这台本地算力安排好，我们就开始着手怎么让手机能连接到电脑。就像 Codex 一样，能够在手机上就下达任务，利用本地电脑的环境，执行各种复杂任务。 从流程来看，主要解决的问题就是手机怎样找到 Mac、任务怎样交给 Mac、执行情况怎样回到手机。 为了让手机连进来，Mac 上另外运行一个 HTTPS 代理，代理监听 Mac 的局域网地址，收到手机请求后，转发给本机的 Bridge。 如果以后要在外面用蜂窝网络连接，就可以让手机和 Mac 加入同一个 Tailscale 私有网络，再通过 Tailscale Serve 把 Bridge 提供为私有 HTTPS 服务。 连接后，App 会先检查服务是否正常，再读取会话列表和所选会话的内容。我们选中的会话有一个 sessionId，后续任务就发送到这个会话。 任务进入 Harness 后，由 Mac 上的 Agent 调用本地模型、读取工作区、执行工具，并保存执行记录。手机连接中断不会触发任务取消；只要 Mac 和相关服务继续运行，任务仍由 Harness...

articles.author: Beau Carnes
articles.summary: Most application search setups force a trade-off: settle for simple text filters, or manage a separate search cluster like Elasticsearch with complex synchronization pipelines. In a new video course on the freeCodeCamp.org YouTube channel, I demonstrate how to run an entire production-grade search pipeline inside PostgreSQL. By pairing lexical keyword matching with dense vector embeddings in a single database, you eliminate external dependencies while preserving ACID guarantees for your search index. Search queries usually demand two different retrieval behaviors. Exact queries like "Apollo 13" require precise keyword matching, which keyword engines handle best. articles.summary: 原创 邓哲敏 2026-10-21 19:30 广东 IROS 2026 最佳论文启示录：没有长记忆的机器人，终将被淘汰。 作者丨邓哲敏 编辑丨齐铖湧 本月初在匹兹堡闭幕的 IROS 2026 将最佳论文奖颁给了 LT-Mem，这项研究让机器人重访同一空间时，能完整保留每个物体的位置变迁史，而非仅仅记住最新一次看到的样子。评委会从近两千篇收录论文中选中它，想必不仅是认可其扎实的工作，也是代表学界宣告：具身长记忆（long-term embodied memory）已经从一个工程补丁，变成了机器人领域公认的科学问题。从实际角度考虑，通用机器人要规模化落地，需要以小时、天乃至周为单位持续运行，而不只是几分钟。没有长记忆，每次相遇都是初次见面，机器人只是一个个孤立的单次动作执行器；有了长记忆，它才能从一次性工具变成可以长期上岗的同事。但解决这件事远不是扩大上下文窗口那么简单：持续涌入的多模态数据既无法全部存储，也无法全部检索；现实世界还在不断变化，新的观察既不能简单覆盖旧的，也不能无序堆叠；更棘手的是，一条错误的记忆会在之后的决策里被反复调用，错误由此层层放大。记忆如何写入、如何留证、如何纠错，都是需要被正面回答的问题，靠调几个工程参数解决不了。AI科技评论注意到，在这一方向被顶会加冕的数月前，国内具身初创公司贝塔无限就已坐上牌桌。今年五月，贝塔的联合创始人陶帅在采访中明确表示：长效、多模态、时空记忆的缺失，是他们首先要重点突破的方向。随后，团队陆续发布 BetaMem 全时空多模态记忆架构、世界动作模型 BetaWAM 0.1、首款机器人多米。10 月 20 日，团队把 BetaMem 的写入学习、证据管理和自我改进机制写成了系统的方法与实验，挂上 arXiv。论文交出的成绩单颇为亮眼：BetaMem 采用 9B 开源模型生成记忆，在...

articles.title: 小米神秘新车曝光！SU9 LUX 进军行政轿车市场，还会有一台 SU7 LUX？
articles.author: 李华
articles.summary: 又一辆小米新车被拍到了。 不得不说，小米汽车的辨识度还是很高的，即便身披伪装，大家也能一眼认出这是一辆小米。 虽然车头看着和 SU7 差不多，但把视线移到侧面就能发现，这辆车的车身比例发生了明显的变化，后门被拉长了许多，后三角窗的面积也随之扩大。 结合 SU7 4997mm 的车长估算，这辆新车的车长大概率会超过 5.2 米，轴距也将达到 3.1 米左右。 实际上，这辆车在两个月之前就被人拍到过，当时许多人都以为它是现款 SU7 的长轴距版本。毕竟吐槽 SU7 后排空间的人确有不少，小米多推出一个「SU7 L」也合情合理。 然而，国家知识产权局商标局的公开信息推翻了这个叫法——小米在今年 2 月申请的一个新商标正式获批，名为「XIAOMI SU9 LUX」。 可以看到，小米没有沿用简单加后缀「L」的常规做法，而是将新车划入了数字 9 所代表的旗舰序列。 LUX 取自英文 Luxury，代表豪华与舒适。5.2 米左右的车长让后轮转向成了底盘的必要配置，有了后轮协同偏转，这种体型的大型轿车在狭窄地库泊车或者掉头时，转弯半径会明显缩短，日常通勤中的笨重感也会有所降低。 其实不只是 SU9 LUX，小米在豪华这条产品线上还准备了另外一手，那就是小米 SU7 LUX。 现款 SU7 的底盘设定硬朗，路感反馈清晰，过弯支撑性强，受到许多驾驶爱好者的认可，但也让部分追求平顺代步的用户产生顾虑。 SU7 LUX 大概率会保持现款车型的尺寸框架，主要通过重新标定悬架阻尼、加强隔音、升级更细腻的内饰材质，来提升整车的乘坐质感。 当然，都用上「Luxury」这个后缀了，它的价格大概率也得上去一些。至于 SU9 LUX 这辆「9 系旗舰」，它的售价预计会进入 35 万至 40 万元这一区间。 最终的答案，等到明年 4 月的上海车展，应该就能揭晓了。...

articles.title: Adobe 大改 Photoshop 滤镜逻辑
articles.summary: 少数派 2026-10-21 14:40 广东 10 月 21 日消息，科技媒体 Digital Camera World 昨日（10 月 20 日）发布博文，报道称 Adobe 正重新设计 Photoshop 的滤镜工作方式，现有方案像是「把滤镜印到照片上」，而新机制则是「把滤镜变成一个可随时移动、调节和撤回的效果层」。在目前版本的 Photoshop 中，用户选择某个滤镜后，通常需要先选中一个图层，再在弹出的设置窗口中调整参数并点击确认。滤镜效果随后会被直接应用到该图层的像素上。如果用户之后想改强度、颜色或范围，往往要重新打开滤镜、撤销操作，或借助历史记录回退；若只想让效果作用于画面局部，还需要复制图层、创建选区或添加蒙版。新版机制则把滤镜变成一种更接近图层的独立效果。用户可以在图层面板中把滤镜拖到指定图层上，例如只把高斯模糊应用到背景层，而让人物主体保持清晰。滤镜参数也会从弹窗转移到「属性」面板，用户可以在画布上实时看到变化，并随时调整强度、位置、大小、颜色等设置。如果效果不理想，不必破坏原始照片，用户可以直接修改、隐藏、删除或更换滤镜，更容易实现局部模糊、胶片漏光、镜头光斑等效果，也更适合需要反复尝试风格的后期工作流。Adobe 也在演示 Photoshop AI Assistant 的另一项能力：用户可让 AI 创建自定义滤镜，例如镜头光斑或雨滴效果，并要求其附带可调节的滑块。不过，漏光滤镜本身并不依赖生成式 AI。Adobe 表示，相关更新预计将在今年晚些时候开始推送。 跳转微信打开

articles.title: 回答质量很高，为什么仍错过接话机会？SocialOmni 的多模态社交交互评测
articles.summary: 原创 谢天宇 2026-10-21 13:48 江苏 从“能回答”走向“能参与” 作者：谢天宇（厦门大学），SocialOmni 论文作者一道问答题可以由答案判断对错，多人对话却还要考虑回答发生在什么时候。若只评价模型已经开口的回复，那些错过大多数接话机会的模型也可能得到漂亮的质量分。SocialOmni 将说话人归属、介入判断和自然续写放到同一套诊断视角下，并公开逐条回答，让我们能进一步追问：一个分数究竟反映了什么？一场讨价还价终于结束了。对方已经说了“好吧，拿去吧”，接下来，穿绿色衣服的女士该怎么回应？一个模型接道：“很高兴与你做生意。”另一个模型却说：“来吧，我连公文包也一起给你。”第二句话并不离题，语法也没有问题。公文包确实在前面的谈判中出现过。问题在于，交易已经谈妥，它却把之前的条件重新说了一遍。这是 SocialOmni 公开案例里的一段真实评测。它让我们看到，多模态模型的困难有时并不是不知道画面里有什么，或者听不懂一句话的意思，而是没有跟上对话正在发生的变化：谁在说话，现在轮到谁，这句话之后应该怎样接。如果我们希望音视频助手自然地参与讨论，而不只是等着用户发来一道题，这些看似琐碎的判断就无法绕过。图 1：同一段对话中，Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 给出了一句成交收尾；Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus 重复了前面的加码条件。三位评委对前者均给出 100 分，对后者分别给出 25、0、25 分。这个例子展示的是一次具体的接话差异，完整结果可在项目主页查看。论文：SocialOmni: Benchmarking Audio-Visual Social Interactivity in Omni Models 项目与最新榜单：https://mac-automl.github.io/SocialOmni/...

articles.title: AI Agent学会自我进化！微软与UCSB新研究：自己读论文、改代码
articles.summary: 机器之心 2026-10-21 12:01 北京 AI Agent 能否像研究人员一样，从论文中学习？最近两年，大语言模型的能力不断提升，围绕模型构建的 AI Agent 也逐渐能够处理复杂的任务。从调用工具、操作软件，到规划和执行多步骤工作流，Agent 从处理简单的问答，走向能够独立解决长程复杂工具调用的任务。与此同时，每天也都有很多新的 agent 领域的 preprint 公开在 arXiv 中。但一个现实问题随之出现：当 Agent 遇到能力瓶颈时，我们该如何让它变得更好？最直接的办法是训练更强的模型。然而，Agent 的表现并不完全取决于底层模型。工具如何调用、上下文如何管理、经验如何复用，以及任务如何规划，都会影响最终的执行效果。这些围绕模型运行的软件系统，通常被称为 Agent Harness。近期，Meta Harness 等研究开始探索自动优化 Harness：让一个 Coding Agent 分析任务执行中的失败，再尝试修改 Harness 的代码，并通过实验寻找更好的版本。这种方式已经展现出一定潜力，但也存在一个明显的局限：Coding Agent 提出的改进，很大程度上依赖于自身 Backbone 模型已有的知识，以及此前观察到的失败案例。如果一个问题还没出现，或者模型本身不知道某种更好的解决方法，它就很难主动探索相应的改进方向。人类研究人员面对类似问题时，通常会阅读最新论文，了解其他研究者提出的方法，再尝试将这些方法应用到自己的系统中。那么，能否让 Agent 也具备这样的能力？近日，来自 UCSB 和微软的研究团队提出了 ScholarEvolve，尝试将阅读研究文献、实现算法、评估效果这一研究过程自动化，让最新的学术成果能够直接参与 Agent Harness 的演化。论文： Learning from Research: Toward...

articles.title: Commanding at the Speed of Sound: Audio-Centric Referring Expression Segmentation for Aerial Scenes
articles.author: Fan Liu; Ziyun Chen; Yijun Wang; Chuanyi Zhang; Liang Yao; Yuexuan An; Xiang Gu; Pai Peng
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Referring expression segmentation (RES) aims to localize targets at the pixel level guided by human instructions. However, current models predominantly follow a text-centric paradigm that treats discrete text as the primary interaction medium for these human instructions. This assumption is especially limiting in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, where rapid response, hands-free operation, and natural communication are often critical. In this paper, we reconstruct UAV referring expression segmentation through an audio-centric perspective. Grounded in information theory, we demonstrate that raw audio provides a higher upper bound for extracting rich semantic features than transcribed text. To achieve this, we construct an...

articles.title: Exploring Representation Autoencoders for Text-to-Audio Generation
articles.author: Bernardo V. Miranda (S2A, IDS), Hugo Malard (S2A, IDS), Ga\"el Richard (S2A, IDS), Mathieu Fontaine (LTCI, IP Paris), Slim Essid (IDS, S2A, LTCI)
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Representation autoencoders (RAE), created by pairing a frozen pretrained self-supervised learning (SSL) encoder with a trained decoder, have recently demonstrated state-of-the-art performance on image generation. Their use in the audio domain, however, remains limited: text-to-audio (TTA) models are typically trained in the latent space of dedicated autoencoders where the encoder and the decoder are trained jointly with reconstruction objectives. This paper presents a study on audio representation autoencoders (AuRA) and their applicability to general audio TTA. We train decoders for two pretrained SSL audio encoders and evaluate their reconstruction quality against autoencoders used by recent TTA systems. After obtaining decoders for the...

articles.title: TRACE: Trustworthy Reasoning from Acoustic Cues and Evidence
articles.author: Giovana Morais; Yujin Kim; Atilay Kucukoglu; Magdalena Fuentes
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce TRACE (Trustworthy Reasoning from Acoustic Cues and Evidence), a benchmark for diagnosing the reliability of large audio-language models (LALMs) by revealing when, and under what acoustic conditions these models behave untrustworthily. Existing benchmarks primarily measure whether a model produces the correct answer, but correctness alone cannot determine whether the answer is grounded in acoustic evidence or instead reflects language and contextual priors. TRACE evaluates model behavior along three complementary dimensions: (1) task performance, whether the answer is correct; (2) evidence alignment, whether the model is attending to the audio regions required to answer the question; and (3) robustness, whether answers and...

articles.title: Beyond Two Tracks: Speaker-Anchored Full-Duplex Dialogue Recovery
articles.author: Yuxuan Chen; Yang Xiao; Jack Sun; Chak Sun; Brick Li; Sam
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spoken interaction is moving from alternating turns to full-duplex conversation, where an agent listens while speaking. Learning this coordination requires natural dialogue with persistent speaker-resolved tracks, a data requirement that remains difficult to satisfy at scale. Generative recovery offers a route from ordinary recordings, but recovering two voices is not enough: their track assignments can drift as the conversation unfolds. We address this missing link with speaker-anchored routing before diffusion: a 1.84M-parameter module matches the separator's coarse streams to fixed enrollment identities and orders them before a frozen generator reconstructs the speech, without retraining the generator or altering the reconstructed audio....

articles.title: Steering intonational tunes in text-to-speech synthesis
articles.author: Juan Pablo Vigneaux; Jennifer Cole
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-speech systems built on residual vector quantization often generate audio in two stages: a transformer backbone emits the first level of each frame's token stack, and a smaller depth model generates the rest autoregressively. We ask which components of such a model are responsible for prosodic intonation, more precisely for generating the English nuclear tune (for instance, the falling pitch melody that distinguishes an assertion from a question's rising melody), and whether interventions on those components can be used to control intonation. Prompt-based control mostly fails; only a final question mark is a reliable lever. Interchange interventions in CSM and S2 locate the tune: the backbone's hidden state carries it to the waveform...

articles.title: MiCLA: Mixture-to-Constituent Latent Alignment for Polyphonic Audio Representation Learning
articles.author: Kohei Yamamoto; Kosuke Okusa
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world audio typically contains concurrent sound events, yet standard self-supervised methods treat each clip as an isolated training unit without explicitly modeling mixture--constituent relationships. We propose Mixture-to-Constituent Latent Alignment (MiCLA), a two-stage self-supervised pre-training framework that uses synthetic log-mel mixing to align mixture representations with their constituent clips. Stage 1 structures single-clip representations via masked self-distillation and contrastive regularization. articles.title: PhonoBridge: Error-Aware Phoneme-Mediated EMG-to-Text Reconstruction
articles.author: Wen Qiu; Jiacheng Zhang; Xuanda Chen; Siqi Cai; Haizhou Li
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electromyography (EMG) provides a non-invasive means of decoding silently articulated speech into text, but accurate decoding remains challenging due to limited availability of paired EMG-text data. We introduce PhonoBridge, a two-stage framework comprising a channel-aware EMG-to-phoneme frontend and a large language model (LLM) backend for text reconstruction. The frontend is trained on paired EMG-text data that consists of channel-wise feature extraction, cross-channel fusion, and electrode embeddings. With phonemes as the intermediate representation, we expand the backend's training data by converting LibriSpeech transcripts into phoneme-text pairs without additional EMG recordings. To adapt the LLM to frontend noise, we introduce...

articles.title: SLM-SS: Token-Based Speech Separation with Speech Language Models
articles.author: Chenda Li; Tianhua Li; Yiming Chen; Wei Wang; Jiahe Wang; Xin Zhou; Yanmin Qian
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speech separation (SS) has witnessed substantial progress in recent years with the advent of neural network-based methods, achieving notable improvements on signal-level evaluation metrics. Existing speech separation systems are mostly optimized with signal-level objectives, and often yield outputs that are acceptable in waveform metrics but suboptimal for intelligibility-sensitive downstream tasks. To address this gap, we propose SLM-SS, a token-based generative speech separation framework that models multi-talker mixtures with speech language models. We first discretize clean speech into multi-codebook token sequences with neural codecs and serialize multi-speaker targets via Serialized Output Training (SOT). An encoder-decoder...

articles.title: APRIL: Ambiguity-Aware Expert Routing for Respiratory Sound Domain-Incremental Learning
articles.author: Xinhong Li; Weiping Tu
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated respiratory sound classification enables continuous, non-invasive respiratory assessment, yet long-term deployment remains challenging due to domain shifts from evolving recording devices and acquisition periods. When privacy and governance regulations prohibit replaying historical data, sequential learning easily overwrites previously acquired knowledge. Preserving dedicated domain experts prevents parameter interference, but selecting the correct expert at inference is difficult under overlapping acoustic distributions and absent domain labels. articles.title: LoCA: Local Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of Autoregressive Flow-Matching TTS
articles.author: Jie Liu; Junyu Zhou; Junhao Zhong; WeiSen Tang; Rukai Cai; Haoyue Zhan; Ruiqi Xing; Ling Long
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning can improve text-to-speech synthesis through feedback on generated speech. However, sentence-level rewards do not identify local errors, while signed regression updates can lead to excessive fitting or repulsion of sampled outputs. We propose LoCA (Local Credit Assignment) for autoregressive flow-matching text-to-speech. LoCA uses ASR-based text alignment to locate content errors in generated speech and redistribute sentence-level advantages across acoustic frames. To improve training stability, we introduce reference-relative positive and negative thresholds that limit continued fitting and repulsion. Experiments on VoxCPM2 show that LoCA reduces sample-weighted content error on a multilingual CV3 evaluation subset by...

articles.title: Slots Are Not Speakers: Training-Free Speaker Linking for Frozen Streaming Diarizers
articles.author: Aditya Srinivas Menon; Kumarmanas Nethil; Kavya Manohar
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a causal, training-free linker that allows a frozen streaming diarizer to track more speakers than it has output slots. Streaming end-to-end diarizers such as Streaming Sortformer emit a fixed number N of concurrent speaker slots. Above N speakers, they keep detecting speech but reuse slots across people, because N bounds how many speakers the model can express at once, not how many it will meet. The linker uses only the host's slot posteriors and the audio. It keeps the frames where one slot is active, splits each slot where the speaker changes, embeds each piece with an off-the-shelf speaker encoder, and matches it against a bank of speakers seen so far. articles.title: Uncovering Audio-Text Alignment in Large Audio-Language Models through Cross-Modal Concept Neurons
articles.author: Tzu-Quan Lin; Chih-Kai Yang; Yi-Cheng Lin; Hao Tang; Hung-yi Lee
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the language model backbone is pretrained on text alone, large audio-language models (LALMs) can, to a great extent, recognize acoustic attributes, such as emotion, speaker gender, and spoken language. However, it is unclear how the audio representation is integrated, if at all, with the other text representation before the model produces text. We hypothesize that there is a shared subspace where the audio and text representations are aligned. To test this hypothesis, we identify cross-modal neurons that are responsible for representing both audio and text. We find alignment between audio and text neurons to various degrees across three LALMs and four acoustic attribute types. Causal interventions, steering and deactivating the...

articles.title: Improved automatic speech-based cognitive assessment using neuropsychologically calibrated diagnostic labels
articles.author: Madhurananda Pahar; Caitlin Illingworth; Adam Hampshire; Peter J Hellyer; Agata J Hampshire; Daniel Blackburn; Annalena Venneri; Heidi Christensen
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although automatic detection of cognitive impairment from conversational speech is a promising way, it becomes less accurate, as large real-world datasets often contain unreliable diagnostic labels due to self-referral and limited clinical verification, and here we investigated whether neuropsychologically calibrated diagnostic relabeling improves it. We analysed 138 hours of conversational speech from 720 participants, recalibrating unreliable diagnostic labels using attention, executive function, and memory performance via external clinical thresholds, Gaussian, and normative z-score calibration. articles.title: WaveCommitments: Private and Verifiable Speech-Agent Marketplaces
articles.author: Oguzhan Baser; Kaan Kale; Sriram Vishwanath; Sandeep Chinchali
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern speech systems are evolving into ecosystems of autonomous speech agents that speak together, negotiate, and trade assets such as embeddings, spectrograms, or raw data. In such markets, sellers cannot reveal assets for evaluation due to privacy constraints, and buyers cannot price what they cannot test. Thus, we open-source WaveCommitments, an end-to-end design that pairs confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley inside a trusted execution environment with multivariate polynomial commitments. It enables selective openings and tamper-evident provenance to prove that a delivered asset matches the valuation while hiding everything else. Our extensive experiments across three known datasets and various tasks with state-of-the-art...

articles.title: Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition with Bidirectional Audio--Text Cross-Attention
articles.author: TingTing Gu; JinCheng Luo; WenQiu Guo
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are subtle behavioural states that can be expressed through both what a person says and how it is spoken. This paper presents an audio--text framework for video-level A/H recognition. Full-video transcripts and speech waveforms are encoded using pre-trained multilingual BERT and wav2vec~2.0, respectively, and projected into a shared representation space. Two stacked bidirectional cross-attention blocks allow linguistic tokens to attend to acoustic frames and acoustic frames to attend to linguistic context without requiring explicit temporal alignment. articles.author: Eulalie Thiombiano; Martha Larson; Vincent Colotte; Emmanuel Vincent
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Currently, voice-related privacy risks are studied under the assumption that the attacker has access only to spoken audio. In contrast, real-world collections often pair the speech signal with side information; yet to our knowledge, no publicly available dataset provides sufficiently detailed and directly linkable speech and side-information pairs to evaluate the combined risk. We propose a distribution-constrained method to build a semi-synthetic dataset and study singling out risk when geographic side information is assumed to accompany anonymized speech. articles.title: Mixture of Phonetic Experts Based Low-Rank Adaptation of Conformer Models for Accented English Speech Recognition
articles.author: Santosh Dahal; Anmol Guragain; Tianchi Liu; Luis Fernando D'Haro; Kiran Chandra Dahal
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. articles.title: Disentangling Depression from Cognitive Decline in Elderly Speech Using Concurrent Clinical Assessments
articles.author: Woori Jeon; Seunghee Ha; Sang-Kyu Lee; Ji Hye Yoon; Tae-Jin Yoon; Seung Jin Lee; Woojae Han; Jungmin So
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detecting depression from speech in elderly patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is complicated by overlapping acoustic effects of cognitive decline. Without disentangling these, classifiers risk learning cognitive rather than depression-specific patterns. We present a Korean elderly speech corpus of 89 MCI speakers collected over three years with concurrent depression (SGDS) and cognitive (MMSE) assessments. Both linear mixed-effects models and partial correlations identify the same pattern: of seven feature groups, only formant features are associated with depression after controlling for cognitive function, while widely used F0 features carry no signal. articles.title: PW-Pruning: Phase-Aware Expert Selection for Speech-Centric Omni-Modal Models
articles.author: Junjie Cao; Fengping Tian; Wenjie Zhou; Xuanfan Ni; Chenyang Lyu; Siyou Liu; Longyue Wang; Weihua Luo
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse routing reduces per-token computation but leaves the full expert bank resident in memory. We propose PW-Pruning, a phase-aware extension of DO-ACP that constructs separate importance-weighted kernels for acoustic-prefill and teacher-forced answer tokens, then combines phase-weighted log-determinant marginal gains to select one static expert bank. articles.title: ShlokaDhara: A Multi-Speaker Sanskrit Speech Corpus for Learning Meter-Aware Prosody in Text-to-Recitation
articles.author: Harshal Kausadikar; Onkar Kishor Susladkar; Prathmesh Santosh Choudhari; Vedangi Deepak Deshpande; Ismini Lorentzu; Sparsh Mittal
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sanskrit verse recitation is governed by $\textit{Chandas}$, a strict prosodic framework defined by rhythmic $\textit{Laghu}$ (light) and $\textit{Guru}$ (heavy) syllables. Because existing Sanskrit speech datasets prioritize ASR or conversational TTS, they lack the metrical fidelity required for authentic verse synthesis. We introduce $\textbf{\textit{ShlokaDhara}}$, a 43-hour, multi-speaker Sanskrit speech corpus capturing diverse meters, recitation styles, and melodic variations. We specifically focus on $\textit{Text-to-Recite}$, a synthesis task explicitly requiring both prosodic accuracy and metrical correctness. articles.title: Point2Acoustic: Efficient Room Acoustic Parameter Estimation from 3D Geometry and Material Properties
articles.author: Xun Gao; Raksha Ramakrishna; Tommy Falk; Werner de Bruijn
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scene-adaptive immersive audio rendering requires rapid estimation of acoustic parameters that reflect the surrounding environment. For repeated runtime scene updates, performing a detailed geometric-acoustic simulation for every update can be computationally costly. We present Point2Acoustic, a learning-based framework for direct estimation of six-band reverberation time ($RT_{60}$) and reverberant-to-direct ratio (RDR) from 3D scene geometry and acoustic material properties. Each scene is represented by a surface-sampled point cloud with spatial coordinates and frequency-dependent absorption and scattering coefficients, and encoded using PointNet or PointNet++. articles.title: Preference-Aware Pareto Steering for Multi-Task Speech LLMs
articles.author: Liuyuan Jiang; Vishal Sunder; Samuel Thomas; Brian Kingsbury; Jeff Kuo; Lisha Chen; George Saon
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech large language models (LLMs) perform multiple tasks, including automatic speech recognition (ASR), timestamp prediction (TS), and speech translation (ST). Joint training of speech LLMs creates task trade-offs, yet standard training with fixed loss weights does not generally control the resulting trade-off according to deployment preferences. To address this, we propose Endpoint-Anchored Preference-Aware Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front (EA-SURF), an a priori method that adapts scalarization weights so that the resulting task trade-off reflects the desired preference. articles.title: You Are the Trigger: Speaker-Activated Backdoors
articles.author: Nata\v{s}a Kr\v{c}o; Euodia Dodd; Peter Romov; Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech models are increasingly used as an interface to AI systems, from transcription tools to voice agents. Existing audio backdoors require an attacker to introduce triggers at inference time. We study a different threat model in which the attacker compromises the model during fine-tuning but has no access to the victim's inference-time inputs. We introduce the Speaker-Activated Backdoor (SAB) setting, in which a target speaker's natural voice serves as the trigger. We develop a two-phase fine-tuning method that first makes speaker identity more accessible and then binds the target speaker to an attacker-chosen payload. articles.author: Jaeyeon Kim; Heeseung Yun; Sang Hoon Woo; Chao-Han Huck Yang; Gunhee Kim
articles.summary: arXiv:2508.20976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) extend language understanding into the auditory domain, yet their ability to perform low-level listening, such as pitch and duration detection, remains underexplored. However, low-level listening is critical for real-world, out-of-distribution tasks where models must reason about unfamiliar sounds based on fine-grained acoustic cues. To address this gap, we introduce the World-of-Whale benchmark (WoW-Bench) to evaluate low-level auditory perception and cognition using marine mammal vocalizations. We use marine mammal vocalizations as out-of-distribution sound events to better assess models' low-level listening and so that the models do not rely on prior knowledge of the sound events. articles.title: Speaker-Disentangled Remote Speech Detection of Asthma and COPD Exacerbations
articles.author: Yuyang Yan; Sami O. Simons; Visara Urovi
articles.summary: arXiv:2605.16878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Early detection of exacerbations in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is important for timely intervention. Speech has emerged as a promising tool for continuous, non-invasive respiratory disease monitoring. However, speech signals inherently carry speaker-identifiable attributes that may dominate model predictions, which may compromise both diagnostic accuracy and patient privacy. We propose an adversarial learning architecture that disentangles pathology-related acoustic patterns from speaker-identifiable attributes through gradient reversal-based training. To enhance clinical interpretability, we employ SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify the contributions of acoustic features to pathology-related...

articles.title: TTS-Q: Speaker-Aware Post-Training Quantization of Text-to-Speech Diffusion Transformers
articles.author: Xiaoqin Feng; Yuqi Li; Weilun Feng; Yi-Cheng Lin; Kai Li; Xianglong Wang; Kuo Yang; Chuanguang Yang; Yingli Tian; Wei Li; Zhongwei Cheng; Lin Chen
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.12474v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) can clone a voice from seconds of audio. Yet the quality comes from billion-parameter diffusion transformers whose size and multi-step sampling put them out of reach of the on-device, assistive, and real-time applications that need them most. Post-training quantization (PTQ) shrinks such models without retraining, but it has been built for language and vision, not speech. At 4 bits, a strong quantizer leaves intelligibility close to full precision but consistently erodes speaker timbre, so error rates stay low while the voice drifts from the target speaker. We ask why quantization hurts speech, where the damage lives, and whether it can be repaired without retraining. To find out, we run the first 4-bit...

articles.title: SpikCTU: A Compact Spiking Network with Adaptive Recurrent Computation for Speech Command Recognition
articles.author: Li Jin; Jiang Wenbin; Chen Tao; Wen Fei
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.14594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks offer event-driven, energy-efficient computation for speech command recognition, yet most existing methods follow fixed computation paths, allocating redundant computation to easy samples while providing limited insight into how evidence evolves during inference. To address these challenges, we introduce SpikCTU, a compact spiking network with adaptive recurrent computation for speech command recognition. Specifically, a hybrid spiking embedding module preserves continuous input information alongside spike features to construct a fixed temporal memory. A shared Continuous Thinking Unit (CTU) repeatedly reads this memory using keys derived from spikes and continuous values, and updates a binary recurrent state with...

articles.title: Binaural Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation
articles.author: Saijun Wang; Guanfeng Tang; Hongbo Zhao; Zhicheng Lei; Yutong Zhang; Wei Ye; Rui Fan
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.32180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Audio-visual segmentation (AVS) aims to segment sounding objects at the pixel level by integrating auditory and visual cues. However, existing methods are predominantly developed under the monaural setting and primarily rely on cross-modal semantic correspondence, which limits their ability to distinguish visually similar instances of the same semantic class. In contrast, humans naturally exploit binaural hearing, where interaural differences and direction-dependent acoustic filtering introduced by the head and pinnae provide physically grounded spatial cues for accurate sound source localization. Motivated by this observation, we introduce binaural audio-visual instance segmentation (BiAVIS), a new task that leverages synchronized...

articles.title: ELARSpeech: A 30K-Hour Dataset Across 675 Underrepresented Languages for Long-Tail Multilingual Speech Technologies
articles.author: Sangmin Lee; Yejin Jeon; David Ifeoluwa Adelani
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.19388v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Massively multilingual speech modeling has made remarkable progress in recent years, yet existing training resources and benchmarks still underrepresent much of the linguistic long tail. To address this gap, we introduce ELARSpeech, a large-scale multilingual speech resource comprising 30,202 hours of speech across 675 underrepresented languages, curated from the Endangered Languages Archive. Combining human-annotated and unlabeled recordings, the corpus spans diverse recording conditions, domains, and language families. Beyond corpus construction, our experiments show how ELARSpeech supports extending ASR and TTS capabilities to diverse underrepresented languages, with further benefits from pseudo-labeling unlabeled data. articles.title: The Impact of Side Information on Voice Privacy
articles.author: Eulalie Thiombiano; Martha Larson; Vincent Colotte; Emmanuel Vincent
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Currently, voice-related privacy risks are studied under the assumption that the attacker has access only to spoken audio. In contrast, real-world collections often pair the speech signal with side information; yet to our knowledge, no publicly available dataset provides sufficiently detailed and directly linkable speech and side-information pairs to evaluate the combined risk. We propose a distribution-constrained method to build a semi-synthetic dataset and study singling out risk when geographic side information is assumed to accompany anonymized speech. We instantiate it using the English portion of Mozilla Common Voice and the 2021 UK Census, under ignorant and semi-informed attackers, and introduce a conditional reference that...

articles.title: Omni-Woodpecker: Hallucination Correction via Evidence-Prior Rebalancing for Omni LLMs
articles.author: Zijian Liu; Chaoyou Fu; Yan Yang; Caifeng Shan; Ran He
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states....

articles.title: Revealing Inter-Channel Modality Discriminability: Channel Selective Interaction Fusion Network for Optical-SAR Object Detection
articles.author: Haojie Li; Yuanfei Huang; Lingfei Song; Jia Li; Lizhi Wang
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27757v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and optical imagery provide complementary structural and appearance information for remote sensing object detection. However, substantial cross-modal discrepancies and indiscriminate channel interaction inevitably introduce redundant or conflicting features. Since different feature channels encode heterogeneous semantic information and contribute unequally to cross-modal fusion, selectively highlighting task-relevant channels while suppressing redundant ones is essential. To address this issue, we propose the Channel Selective Interaction Fusion Network (CSIF-Net), which performs selective channel-level cross-modal interaction. articles.title: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content
articles.author: David Fischinger, Marcel Hasenbalg, Silvia Poletti, Davide Antonutti, Mina Sch\"utz, Lam Pham, Justin Ilyes, P\'eter Rjabcsenk\'o, Simon Freitter, Martin Boyer
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid progress of generative artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in manipulated multimedia content, including synthetic faces, forged videos, AI-generated images, fake audio, and locally edited images. Existing detection approaches are typically designed for a single manipulation type, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios involving heterogeneous media sources. In this work, we present the Media Intelligence Platform (MIP), a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis. articles.author: Fengyun Zhang
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One-to-many ultra-wideband (UWB) transport can disseminate shared audio blocks without replicating a downlink stream for every receiver. Yet common reception does not ensure aligned electrical playback, coincident acoustic arrival, or delivery to an entire receiver group. articles.title: A Survey of Generative Categories and Techniques in Multimodal Generative Models
articles.author: Longzhen Han; Awes Mubarak; Almas Baimagambetov; Nikolaos Polatidis; Thar Baker
articles.summary: arXiv:2506.10016v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal generative models (MGMs) have rapidly expanded beyond text generation to encompass images, music, video, human motion, and 3D objects. This survey categorises six primary text-conditioned generative modalities and examines how four techniques, namely self-supervised learning, mixture of experts, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and chain-of-thought prompting, are adapted across them, distinguishing shared mechanisms from experimentally supported benefits. We organise evaluation around faithfulness, compositionality, and robustness, and interpret evidence within each study's protocol. articles.title: Unified Agentic Video Editing Across Levels of Complexity and Creativity
articles.author: Surabhi S. Nath; Kim Ferres; Milan Petrovi\'c; Lion Schulz
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.12769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Editing is a core component of video production, requiring creative planning and decisions under multiple constraints. Here, we report methods for agentic tooling for automated video editing across three tasks varying in editorial goal, complexity and creativity, namely scene previews, video summaries and cinematic trailers. We evaluate the outputs and discuss implications for automation and agency.

articles.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.24791v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities. Existing methods rely heavily on paired corpora, which are scarce for joint generation and even rarer for editing. Consequently, they are spent learning single-branch generative and editing capabilities that abundant unimodal data could readily teach, rather than on the cross-modal coupling. Furthermore, prevailing systems apply a single shared noise schedule to both modalities, neglecting two critical limitations. articles.title: Disentangling Depression from Cognitive Decline in Elderly Speech Using Concurrent Clinical Assessments
articles.author: Woori Jeon; Seunghee Ha; Sang-Kyu Lee; Ji Hye Yoon; Tae-Jin Yoon; Seung Jin Lee; Woojae Han; Jungmin So
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting depression from speech in elderly patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is complicated by overlapping acoustic effects of cognitive decline. Without disentangling these, classifiers risk learning cognitive rather than depression-specific patterns. We present a Korean elderly speech corpus of 89 MCI speakers collected over three years with concurrent depression (SGDS) and cognitive (MMSE) assessments. Both linear mixed-effects models and partial correlations identify the same pattern: of seven feature groups, only formant features are associated with depression after controlling for cognitive function, while widely used F0 features carry no signal. articles.title: PW-Pruning: Phase-Aware Expert Selection for Speech-Centric Omni-Modal Models
articles.author: Junjie Cao; Fengping Tian; Wenjie Zhou; Xuanfan Ni; Chenyang Lyu; Siyou Liu; Longyue Wang; Weihua Luo
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse routing reduces per-token computation but leaves the full expert bank resident in memory. We propose PW-Pruning, a phase-aware extension of DO-ACP that constructs separate importance-weighted kernels for acoustic-prefill and teacher-forced answer tokens, then combines phase-weighted log-determinant marginal gains to select one static expert bank. articles.title: ShlokaDhara: A Multi-Speaker Sanskrit Speech Corpus for Learning Meter-Aware Prosody in Text-to-Recitation
articles.author: Harshal Kausadikar; Onkar Kishor Susladkar; Prathmesh Santosh Choudhari; Vedangi Deepak Deshpande; Ismini Lorentzu; Sparsh Mittal
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sanskrit verse recitation is governed by $\textit{Chandas}$, a strict prosodic framework defined by rhythmic $\textit{Laghu}$ (light) and $\textit{Guru}$ (heavy) syllables. Because existing Sanskrit speech datasets prioritize ASR or conversational TTS, they lack the metrical fidelity required for authentic verse synthesis. We introduce $\textbf{\textit{ShlokaDhara}}$, a 43-hour, multi-speaker Sanskrit speech corpus capturing diverse meters, recitation styles, and melodic variations. We specifically focus on $\textit{Text-to-Recite}$, a synthesis task explicitly requiring both prosodic accuracy and metrical correctness. articles.title: Point2Acoustic: Efficient Room Acoustic Parameter Estimation from 3D Geometry and Material Properties
articles.author: Xun Gao; Raksha Ramakrishna; Tommy Falk; Werner de Bruijn
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scene-adaptive immersive audio rendering requires rapid estimation of acoustic parameters that reflect the surrounding environment. For repeated runtime scene updates, performing a detailed geometric-acoustic simulation for every update can be computationally costly. We present Point2Acoustic, a learning-based framework for direct estimation of six-band reverberation time ($RT_{60}$) and reverberant-to-direct ratio (RDR) from 3D scene geometry and acoustic material properties. Each scene is represented by a surface-sampled point cloud with spatial coordinates and frequency-dependent absorption and scattering coefficients, and encoded using PointNet or PointNet++. articles.title: pyFDN: A Python Toolbox for Feedback Delay Network Design, Analysis, and Optimization
articles.author: Sebastian J. Schlecht; Facundo Franchino; Jeremy B. Bai
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) provide a compact representation of recursive audio systems for artificial reverberation and decorrelation. Their practical use spans structured matrix design, acoustic decay shaping, numerical simulation, and modal analysis, increasingly combined with differentiable optimization. We present pyFDN, an open-source Python toolbox that brings these operations into a common workflow. The library combines numerical design and analysis routines with block-based time-domain processing and integration with FLAMO for frequency-domain differentiable processing. articles.title: RealComm: Benchmarking and Adapting Audio Deepfake Detection over Real Communication Channels
articles.author: Li Wang; Jindong Wang; Wan Lin; Kunyu Feng; Yufan Lin; Lei Wang; Rizhao Cai; Ce Fang; Jinzhe Xue; Jie Shi; Haizhou Li; Zhizheng Wu
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustic capture, device processing, and transmission coding in real calls jointly alter speech signals and may affect the reliability of audio deepfake detection. To systematically evaluate these effects, we introduce RealComm, a dataset pairing digital speech with recordings of the same utterances transmitted through real mobile calls. The acquisition design covers acoustic and wired injection, handset and speakerphone operation, and caller-side denoising, with bona fide and synthetic speech recorded under matched conditions. The dataset includes RealCommBench for evaluation and RealCommTrain for adaptation. articles.author: Junyu Wang; Tianrui Wang; Meng Ge; Longbiao Wang; Xiaobao Wang; Jianwu Dang
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advancements in large-scale audio classification have been primarily driven by Transformer-based architectures due to their strong capacity in modeling long-range dependencies. However, their inherent quadratic complexity limits scalability and efficiency, especially when processing long or sparsely informative audio streams. Mamba, a recently proposed state space model (SSM), offers a promising alternative by enabling efficient long-range modeling with linear sequence scaling. articles.title: VISH-ASR: Viterbi-Guided Selection of Hotwords for Speech-LLM Contextual ASR

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt-based contextual ASR requires selecting a compact hotword subset from large dynamic inventories, yet existing pre-selection methods rely either on discrete ASR hypotheses that may discard acoustic evidence or on separately trained retrieval models. articles.title: Sound Matching with a Differentiable Karplus-Strong Algorithm

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a self-supervised, event-based sound matching model using a differentiable extended Karplus-Strong algorithm. To avoid relying on external onset and fundamental frequency detectors, we explore training methodologies combining parameter losses on synthetic data with audio losses. articles.author: David Marttila; Rodrigo Diaz; Pablo Tablas De Paula; Ilias Ibnyahya; Chin-Yun Yu
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present two Transformer-based methods for Task A of the 1st DAFx Parameter Estimation Challenge, which requires estimating six effective physical parameters of a synthetic plate-reverb model from its impulse response (IR). Method A2 uses the same encoder to condition a continuous normalizing flow and refines sampled candidates using particle swarm optimisation (PSO) and gradient polishing. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active noise control (ANC) is an established technique for mitigating acoustic noise, successfully implemented in various commercial applications. However, the application of ANC to augmented reality (AR) glasses remains an emerging area, where a key challenge is the lack of a microphone at the user's ear. articles.title: Multimodal Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition with Bidirectional Audio--Text Cross-Attention
articles.author: TingTing Gu; JinCheng Luo; WenQiu Guo
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are subtle behavioural states that can be expressed through both what a person says and how it is spoken. This paper presents an audio--text framework for video-level A/H recognition. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. articles.author: Giovana Morais; Yujin Kim; Atilay Kucukoglu; Magdalena Fuentes
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce TRACE (Trustworthy Reasoning from Acoustic Cues and Evidence), a benchmark for diagnosing the reliability of large audio-language models (LALMs) by revealing when, and under what acoustic conditions these models behave untrustworthily. articles.title: Beyond Two Tracks: Speaker-Anchored Full-Duplex Dialogue Recovery

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spoken interaction is moving from alternating turns to full-duplex conversation, where an agent listens while speaking. Learning this coordination requires natural dialogue with persistent speaker-resolved tracks, a data requirement that remains difficult to satisfy at scale. articles.title: SMART: Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics
articles.author: Xiaoyu Gu; Chencheng Wang; Fuyang Li; Yu Xi; Tao Liu; Jiaoqi Guo; Kai Yu

articles.summary: 数十年来，家庭影院与音乐 Hi-Fi 基本走在两条互不妥协的轨道上：前者追求声场定位与大动态，却长期被困在「电视外设」的单一角色中——电视一关便陷入沉睡。 而后者讲究结像与音色，严守「听音皇帝位」，对布线要求苛刻，且难以融入当下的流媒体与多房间生态。 当流媒体的「快」、黑胶复兴的「慢」以及 HiFi 的「专」同时涌入生活，每多一种发烧爱好，就不得不添置一套专属设备。原本用来喘息放松的居心地，被大大小小的箱体、插线板和三四个互不通用的遥控器生生塞成了小型器材展。 而这恰恰是 Sonos Beam Ultra 让我感兴趣的地方。 它本质是一套基于家庭 Wi-Fi 的声音系统：接上电视，它是支持杜比全景声的回音壁；关掉电视，它通过 Sonos App 聚合主流流媒体服务，遇到朋友临时点歌，它能秒变支持 AirPlay 2 或蓝牙 5.3 的无线音箱；而背部的 USB-C 接口，甚至还给黑胶唱机留出了接入空间。 视觉极尽克制，却在接口与实体交互上做足了加法 Beam Ultra 延续了 Sonos 一贯简约的设计语言，提供黑白两色，表面采用哑光处理。 75 厘米的宽度、6.5 厘米的高度，相较于接近 1.18 米宽的 Arc Ultra，体量显得格外收敛，置于主流的 65-75 英寸电视下方，或者进深狭窄的现代电视柜上，既不会产生喧宾夺主的视觉压迫感，也恰好避开了屏幕下沿。 但这副极简的皮囊之下，Sonos 并没有为了所谓的一体化而砍掉按键，反而在实体交互上做足了加法。 尽管语音和 App 控制已经十分成熟，机身顶部依然保留了丰富的触控区域，比如内凹式音量滑条设计、播放控制按键，在脱离手机或遥控器时，这种直接的物理操作异常顺手。 考虑到朋友做客时的临时点歌需求，机身背部特意增加了一枚独立蓝牙配对键，长按即可直连。苹果用户有便捷的 AirPlay 2，而新增的蓝牙 5.3...

articles.summary: 原创 夕小瑶编辑部 2026-10-21 11:21 北京 这两年大模型圈有一条几乎没人怀疑的信条，Scaling Law。加算力，加参数，加数据，模型就稳定地变强。最要命的是这个所谓的稳定，投进去多少，大概能换回多少，是可以预期的。所以各家模厂才敢成千上万张地买卡、屯卡。其中，砸卡最狠的公司之一 Meta，最近更新了一项进展。GEM 是 Meta 的广告推荐基础模型，大家平时在 Facebook、Instagram 上刷到哪条广告，背后很大程度上就是它在算。最新一代GEM模型，在几千张最新一代 GPU 上训练，总训练计算量是一年前的 4 倍。这么看，推荐系统也开始按大模型的量级砸卡了。说到推荐系统，可能是你每天用得最多、却最少想起的 AI。我列一组数字你就全明白了：2024 年全球数字广告支出大概 7900 亿美元（直白点说这是推荐模型能撬动的商业市场）OpenAI 2024 年全年收入才37 亿美元。今年大模型圈最能赚钱的两家，Anthropic 最新的年化收入大概是 650 亿美元，OpenAI也在几百亿美元的量级，加起来也只是对方的十分之一这个量级。一切技术研究大模型化，这本来不算什么新鲜事。Meta博客里有一句话，还是让我留意了。Meta 说，大模型那种 Scaling Law，放到推荐系统上，并不会自然出现。离钱这么近，旁边又摆着大模型这条现成的路，砸卡是理所当然的事，但是同样是神经网络，同样是砸算力，凭啥一个越砸越聪明，另一个就不太吃这一套？巧的是，这道题，我还真研究过。今年的腾讯广告算法大赛，题目就是这个。我也带着我的 Codex 报了名，奖金嘛，当然是没拿到 QvQ前几天，官方放出了论文，把整场比赛从头到尾复盘了一遍。我这两天把它翻完了，发现它几乎就是在正面回答 Meta...

articles.summary: 原创 阿雅 2026-10-21 11:21 北京 AI for Science，这次是真刀真枪进了实验室。Anthropic 直接对着蝎子的毒素下手了。就在今天，Anthropic公布了一项新研究：一个还没公开的研究版 Claude，在约 64 小时内，自主生成了 318,484 个从头蛋白设计！经过筛选和人工补充，211个 候选被送进实验室，最终 17个 在实验台上真正结合上了蝎子的神经毒素。更关键的是，全部 211 个设计与实验数据，Anthropic 直接全部开源。从读资料、选结构、到调用工具，Claude 几乎独立跑完了传统上需要一整支计算生物团队、耗时数月的工作量。而它用的时间，是 64 小时。◈为什么偏偏盯上蝎毒蝎子蜇人，真不是小事。据 Anthropic 转述的文献估计，全球每年 120 万人以上被蝎蜇伤，死亡超过 3250 例，受害的大多是儿童，大多在医疗资源不够的地区。而传统抗蝎毒血清的制备，至今仍然依赖“给马等动物注射毒液、再提取抗体”的方式：贵、慢，而且覆盖范围有限一个地方的血清，未必能应对另一个地方的蝎毒。于是投资研究机构 Citrini Research 找到 Anthropic，抛出一个比较“外行”的问题：一群没有任何生物学背景的人，能不能靠 Claude，去啃一个真实的公共卫生难题？双方反复打磨提示词，最终把目标锁定在蝎神经毒素上。Claude 要做的，就是一类叫"结合剂"（binder）的小蛋白。打个比方：蝎神经毒素像一把"坏钥匙"，专门插进神经细胞膜上的钠离子通道，让神经疯狂乱放电，严重时直接把人推向心衰、肺水肿。而结合剂，就是一段从零设计的小蛋白，使命只有一个，死死贴住毒素"插钥匙"的那一面，把它彻底封死。◈64小时，Claude全程自主交出30万设计接下来，才是 Claude 真正开始表演的部分。最开始人类只给了 Claude...

articles.summary: 关注前沿科技 2026-10-21 11:02 北京 AI能给出数学证明，不代表人类真正理解了这道题 文章转载于量子位作者：henry陶哲轩和邓煜，也开始「慢科研」了（doge）。“保留那些慢慢做科学、做数学的方式所带来的好处，包括增进理解、建设共同体，让人类持续掌握对一个学科的理解。”就在刚刚，针对商业AI批量发布数学证明引发的争议，两位菲尔兹奖得主坐到一起，在SAIR发布的一场访谈中给出了回应。两人的核心观点是：AI能给出数学证明，不代表人类真正理解了这道题。过去，解决一道数学难题，往往也意味着研究者能够解释证明、提出新问题，并将知识传授给其他人。但如今，当AI开始批量产出证明，「解出来了」和「弄明白了」，可能是两回事。比起AI又解出了多少道题，两人更关心这些证明能否被理解、推导能否被核查，以及数学家能否在此基础上继续探索。访谈中，两人还进一步讨论了数学家与AI该如何分工：哪些繁琐推导可以交给AI，哪些提问、规划和判断能力，仍需要研究者自己培养。这也是两人参与Open Math Model开放数学模型计划的动机之一：让数学共同体参与工具开发，使AI真正服务于数学研究。按照访谈时的进展，团队的新模型仍在筹备，率先推出的是Open Math...

articles.title: 三十而立，奇瑞不想只做一家汽车公司
articles.author: 刘学文
articles.summary: 一家汽车公司，应该把研发资源投入到什么地方？更高效的发动机、更长续航的电池、更聪明的智能驾驶，或者一辆能够卖到全球的汽车？ 这些答案都没错。 在 2026 年的奇瑞全球创新大会上，奇瑞展示了和传统奇瑞一些不太一样的东西：能够载人飞行的 eVTOL、在农田里自主作业的电动拖拉机、走进家庭和医院的人形机器人，甚至还有能够从空气中取水的太阳能汽车。 当然，还有现在最热门的关键词——AI。 10 月 20 日，在奇瑞全球创新大会上，奇瑞董事长尹同跃再次强调奇瑞另一种定位：奇瑞是一家「披着车企马甲」的高科技创新公司。 对于一家即将迎来 30 岁生日、连续 23 年位居中国品牌乘用车出口第一的汽车企业而言，造车本身已经是一门足够庞大的生意，做一家基业长青的汽车公司没有什么不好。 但奇瑞显然不打算止步于此。 这次大会，奇瑞正式公布了「瑶光 2035」战略，目标是从传统汽车制造商，进化为一家以 AI 驱动的全球智能科技公司。 AI 时代，奇瑞想造的不只是汽车，还有大脑 过去几年，汽车行业围绕 AI 展开了一系列的军备竞赛，包括但不限于智能辅助驾驶的研发，自研大模型上车，投资乃至创办一家 AI 公司。 智能驾驶需要更大的模型，智能座舱需要更聪明的助手，汽车制造也在尝试利用 AI 提升研发和生产效率。 但大多数时候，这些 AI 能力仍然分散在不同的业务和产品之中。 奇瑞希望改变这一点。 在本届创新大会上，奇瑞发布了面向物理 AI 的垂类基础大模型 CheryMind。和通用大语言模型不同，CheryMind 并不以聊天、写作作为主要目标，而是试图让 AI 理解物理世界，并且真正参与现实世界中的决策和行动。 支撑这个模型的，是奇瑞积累的 700TB 企业知识、200PB 工程数据、2500 万段教练级驾驶数据，以及 500 万段机器人动作捕捉数据。...

articles.title: 给AI写了800行规则，它反而更不听话了
articles.summary: 原创 刘俊毅 2026-10-21 08:45 广东 关注腾讯云开发者，一手技术干货提前解锁👇开发者公众号专属群聊扫码加入获取更多一手教程、科技前沿报告一个中等复杂度的业务需求，过去从评审到出可体验版本，我们大约要花一个月。现在，多数需求一到两周就能完成，其中编码环节从以天计压缩到了一两个小时。这个变化并不来自换了一个更强的模型。用 AI 写过业务代码的人，大概都经历过这些时刻：会话一长，AI 就忘了前面的约定；换个会话，上周踩过的坑又踩一次。需求在 AI 手里转述几次就走了样，写出来"差不多，但不对"。报错日志、编辑器状态，得人一段段复制给 AI 看。这些问题都不是因为 AI 不会写代码，而是出在代码之外：它不知道自己处在流程的哪一步，记不住过去的教训，也看不到真实的开发环境。AI 会写代码，不等于 AI 能交付。我们最初的解法很直接：写一个流程 Skill，把开发步骤列成清单，让 AI 照着走。可跑起来，AI 总是忘了这步、漏了那步，我们只好不断往里加限制和规则。不到一个月，这份 Skill 从五百多行涨到八百多行，开头还多了五条"铁律"，标题写着"违反任何一条即为失败"，第一条就是"逐步执行，禁止跳步"。结果规则越写越多，AI 反而越不听话：上下文里塞进的东西越多，每条规则分到的注意力就越少，最要紧的那几条反而被埋掉了。后来我们换了思路：不再往上下文里堆规则，而是给 AI 搭一套工程化体系。从第一个业务需求开始，我们一边做需求一边完善它，至今三个多月。回头总结，它可以归结为一句话：流程让 AI 可控，知识库让 AI 能积累，工具让 AI 能接触真实环境。流程、知识库、工具，是这套体系的三根支柱，也是本文的三条主线。01背景1.1...

articles.title: Skipped monorepo deployments no longer count against limits
articles.author: Tom Knickman; Anthony Shew
articles.summary: Deployments that Vercel automatically skips in a monorepo no longer count against your deployment rate limits. Teams with monorepos now get more deployments from the same limits.Vercel skips a project's deployment when its source code and internal dependencies haven't changed, using Turborepo's package graph and lockfile analysis to determine which projects a commit affects. Skipping is enabled by default for new monorepo projects. You can turn it on for existing projects under Build and Deployment in the project's settings.Learn more about skipping unaffected projects and deployment limits. Read more

articles.title: Vol.135｜对话 UDL：AI 眼镜、折叠屏，以及技术背后的设计取舍
articles.author: 佚名
articles.summary: 【本期内容】AI Native 的硬件创业，正在迎来更多新玩家。但技术和制造的门槛降低，并不意味着做出一款好产品变得更加容易。尤其是行业早期缺少成熟产品形态可供参照时，如何定义产品、建立用户认知，反而成了新的挑战。本期节目，我们邀请设计公司UDL合伙人兼工业设计团队负责人胡可人、极客公园品牌创意VP 张山山，以及长期观察消费电子行业的极客公园作者 Alan，展开聊聊 AI 硬件创业潮中，工业设计在产品价值中的新趋势。好的设计，本质上离不开好的产品定义。为什么有些硬件看起来很酷，却很难讲清自己的价值？为什么 Meta 选择优先做好感知，再考虑给眼镜增加一块屏幕？随着开发门槛逐渐降低，设计也不再只是外观与审美的问题，它开始影响产品的差异化竞争、获客效率，甚至订阅转化与长期品牌价值。更有意思的是，AI Native 的设计取舍，尝试将技术隐藏在日常使用体验之中；Even Realities 则通过舍弃摄像头，为智能眼镜换取另一种产品形态。如何在功能、产品形态与使用体验之间找到合理的平衡，是设计师真正需要解决的问题。当 AI 逐渐成为硬件的基础能力，好的产品不再需要依靠外显的「科技感」证明自己。比起不断增加功能，如何让技术以更合理的方式融入日常生活，或许才是这一轮硬件创新中更值得关注的方向。 【嘉宾】张山山｜ 极客公园品牌创意VPAlan｜极客公园作者胡可人｜UDL设计公司合伙人兼工业设计团队负责人【精彩时刻】02:06 AI Native 的产品形态，开发门槛降低之后有哪些变化07:32 Rabbit R1：一个很酷的新硬件，为什么未必能让用户理解它的价值？10:39 Meta 智能眼镜：相比增加显示功能，AI 更需要感知周围世界的能力16:45 工业设计最难的前半程，是如何定义一款产品20:50 iPhone Duo 的设计取舍24:48...

articles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
articles.author: Simon Willison
articles.summary: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise This is very, very bad news: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores. Any software that bundles a list of trusted certificates needs to be updated. This site is tracking software updates via this GitHub repository - Linux distros need to update their ca-certificates packages. In Python world uv 0.13.4 and pip 26.2.2 and certifi 2026.10.19 have been released with upgraded certificate lists. Tags: encryption, https, pip, python, security, uv

articles.title: 中层消失、专家被蒸馏、超级个体单干，公司还需要多少人？｜清华李宁
articles.summary: 原创 博阳 2026-10-21 07:00 北京 不是绝大多数人都能产生突破性创新。但只要创新持续发生，原有的组织和个人就有机会往新的方向走。 穿透技术狂热，追问机器如何重写文明的底层代码。本期是《沸腾之下》系列第06期文｜博阳编辑｜徐青阳老板给你布置了一个两周能做完的任务，但在今天，调用了几个 AI Agent（智能体），你只用一个小时就能搞定。那你会在什么时候交差？清华大学经济管理学院教授、《AI原生组织》作者李宁曾在课堂上问过学生这个问题。大多数人的回答是「两周以后。」这个答案，其实也是另一个问题的答案。为什么个体在借助 AI 狂飙突进时，企业组织却往往感知不到效率的提升？水底的个体早已暗流涌动，水面的组织却依然波澜不惊。公司花重金买了工具、烧了 Token，每个人都似乎变快了，但企业的产出并没有发生质变，反而生产出了海量的重复与冗余。问题的症结，早已不在技术本身，而在于那个运转了两百多年的商业底盘。从亚当·斯密笔下的「制针工厂」开始，现代公司制度的本质就是四个字：拆解与粘合。因为人的能力有边界，我们才把一个完整的目标切碎，发明了工种、部门、职级。之后，再用漫长的会议、复杂的审批和庞大的中层管理，把无数个「局部的人」重新粘合在一起。现在，AI 正在抽走这套逻辑的底座。当写前端的程序员顺手把后端和数据库一并搭好，当五十个人的业务部门可以被三个带着 Agent 的人悄然替代，传统分工的边界正在迅速溶解。但硬币的另一面是，当「生成」变得极其廉价，「验证」却成了新的堰塞湖。几百个 Agent 可以瞬间吞吐出惊人的工作量，却无法替人类分担哪怕一秒钟的犹豫、判断与抉择。组织的分工逻辑，正在从「按工作量切分」，转向更隐秘的「按认知带宽切分」。更深层的博弈发生在水面之下。当企业要求员工把赖以生存的经验写成...

articles.summary: On October 19, 2026, at approximately 17:00 UTC, Cloudflare became aware that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. These certificates were widely trusted by browsers, operating systems, and also within Cloudflare. Because the keys themselves are weak, an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic. This is a serious security incident with implications across the Internet. articles.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
articles.author: Kevin Shabahang
articles.summary: Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history. i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2. This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer. On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second.
